title: If the death certificate is not ready
description: The death is not registered yet, or it was registered late.
opening: A death certificate is given after the death is registered. If that has not happened yet, it can still be done.

official.text: A death should be reported for registration within 21 days. There is no fee if it is reported within that time.
official.confirms: CRS FAQ 1 and 2: "normal period of 21 days"; within it "no fee would be charged".

official.text: If a death is reported after 21 days but within 30 days, it is registered on payment of a late fee.
official.confirms: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, section 13(1): information given after the expiry of the period but within thirty days "shall be registered on payment of such late fee as may be prescribed". Sub-section (1) was not changed by the 2023 or 2026 amendments.

official.text: If it is reported after 30 days but within one year, it needs written permission from the District Registrar or another officer named in the rules, a fee, and a self-attested document.
official.confirms: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (20 of 2023), section 11, new section 13(2): "written permission of the District Registrar or such other authority", fee, "self-attested document". In force from 1 October 2023 (S.O. 4058(E)).

official.text: From 1 October 2026: after one year but within two years, it needs an order from a District, Sub-Divisional or authorised Executive Magistrate. After two years, it needs an order from a Judicial Magistrate of the first class.
official.confirms: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 (12 of 2026), section 2, new section 13(3) and 13(3A); in force from 1 October 2026 by S.O. 5081(E) dated 16 September 2026, printed in the same file.

official.text: A death is registered where it happened, with the registrar of births and deaths for that municipality, panchayat or local area.
official.confirms: CRS FAQ 5: registered "at the place of occurrence of the event"; Registrars appointed for each Municipality, Panchayat or local authority.

official.text: If the death happened at home, the head of the household or the nearest relative there reports it. If it happened in a hospital, the hospital reports it.
official.confirms: CRS FAQ 4: house, head of household or nearest relative; hospital, the medical officer in charge.

official.text: The person who reports the death gets one copy of the certificate free. More copies can be bought for a fee.
official.confirms: CRS FAQ 6: "One free copy" to the informant; "any number of copies" after paying the prescribed fee.

official.text: If you disagree with a decision of the registrar, you can appeal to the District Registrar within 30 days.
official.confirms: CRS FAQ 12, Section 25A: appeal from the Registrar to the District Registrar "within a period of thirty days".

official.text: In Delhi, late registration is handled at the office of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for the area of the death. The papers include an affidavit with the place, date and time of death.
official.confirms: Delhi Revenue Department page: go "To the office of Sub-Divisional Magistrate in whose jurisdiction birth or death took place"; documents include an "Affidavit specifying place, date and time".

suggestions: Ask the registrar which of these applies to you, what papers they need, and what the fee is. Fees can differ by state.
You can start the steps on your checklist that do not need the certificate.
When the certificate is ready, get a few copies. Many places want to keep one.
